design: Prepare the five main cases in order, each once, cold, in a memory store seeded from a read-only production snapshot. A refused preparation stops that case before any image and is retained. When a main case refuses, prepare the next predeclared reserve in order, until five cases are stored or the reserves run out (at most eight preparations). Each stored case renders classical, watercolor and icon twice (variation 1 and 2) with the references production would send, then watercolor twice more with only the style reference removed (control): 8 images per stored case, 40 maximum. Later assemblies must reuse the stored plan with zero text calls.

scoring.method: Images are copied under opaque shuffled names without case, style-control or variation labels beyond what the image shows. Two independent model scorers inspect every image at full resolution; the operator adjudicates and commits before unblinding. Not human acceptance.
perImage: noFormFigure: any face, body, hair, clothing, silhouette or human-shaped figure for God or another no-form subject (yes/no/na)
edges: all four edges painted to the border (full) or any white/unpainted margin or vignette (margin)
extraFigures: framing or unsupported named figures present (yes/no)
coherence: one instant, coherent poses and object states (yes/no)
scoring.gate: Blocker 1 clears only with zero no-form figures in every no-form case image. Blocker 2 clears only if every normal Watercolor image is full-bleed. Results are reported per style and per case; the control shows whether the style reference causes margins. No outcome authorizes activation.

evaluation.measuredBeforeNote: 17.2435676 measured after step 1 plus the full $0.20 cap of the concurrently running step 2, reserved conservatively; the final budget settles from both ledgers.

knownLimitation: Five chosen cases and two repeats per style give descriptive evidence only; this does not replace the full current-candidate visual matrix or human acceptance. Model scorers can miss subtle anatomy or edge artifacts.
